title: Bridged handoff: quarantined hosted routing for dedicated capacity shortfalls
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a bridged handoff policy for routing requests from Dedicated capacity to Hosted when dedicated resources are constrained. The policy introduces a short-term 'quarantine' for any request candidates sent to Hosted: quarantined requests are routed to pre-selected, lower-cost model variants with stricter output validation, tenant-aware rate caps, and temporary scoring/quality flags. Objectives: 1) keep customer apps online when Dedicated is full; 2) preserve SLOs for latency and error rates; 3) contain cost exposure and data-isolation leakage risk by limiting what workloads are eligible for quarantine; 4) provide observability and automatic rollback triggers when quality regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout to 5 tenants: observed <=10% latency increase vs dedicated baseline
Quarantine path enforces per-tenant QPS cap and total cost budget; budget exhaustion triggers fail-fast and tenant fallback to queued retry
Automated quality checks (prompt set eval) detect candidate regression >3% and auto-revert routed traffic within 10 minutes
Tagged telemetry emitted for every handoff: tenant_id, original_model, served_variant, routing_reason, latency_ms, cost_units
Integration tests simulate dedicated saturation and demonstrate no P0 impact to non-eligible tenants
Runbook documented and linked in Console; on-call can manually disable quarantine per region/tenant
comments: 2025-02-10 - Maya Patel: Initial proposal. Problem: Dedicated exhaustion often causes silent latency spikes when we naively spill to Hosted. Proposal: rather than full spill, route a controlled fraction to vetted variants with stricter vetting and temporary flags so customers can opt-in/out.

2025-02-14 - Owen Chen (runtime): We need kernel-level tagging so batch scheduler can keep quarantined requests separated (to avoid cache pollution). Recommend a quarantine tenant tag that's excluded from KV cache priming for 5 minutes.

2025-02-18 - Design review (Amaya Rossi): UX for tenant controls in Console: add a toggle + per-tenant preference page showing quarantine hits and quality deltas. Also add a link to the evaluation prompt set used for automated checks.

2025-02-24 - Security (Hannah Li): Concern about payload routing to Hosted for regulated tenants. We should enforce a tenant allowlist and a strict denylist that is checked before any handoff decision. Recommend 'data_exfil_proof' flag requirement for variants used in quarantine.

2025-03-01 - Jorge Alvarez: Prototype implemented: routing-decider service emits 'quarantine' token with TTL. Added per-tenant soft-QPS cap and hysteresis window (30s) to reduce flapping. Metrics pipeline wired to /dashboards/routing/quarantine-overview (internal).
2025-03-04 - PM feedback (Lena Park): Add cost guardrails: daily per-tenant quarantine spend threshold and a global safety budget that throttles quarantine across tenants when consumed >75%.

2025-03-05 - QA (Ravi Shah): Integration tests running. Found an edge case: when a tenant's dedicated pool is partially evicted, we currently count eligible requests incorrectly; patch in review to incorporate reserved-lane accounting.
2025-03-05 - Jorge Alvarez: PR opened against routing-decider: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/482 (includes quarantine TTL logic and variant scoring hooks).
next_steps: Merge prototype PR and run a 48h canary with 5 pilot tenants
Implement tenant allowlist UI and denylist enforcement in control plane
Add kernel-level request tagging to runtime (separate PR) and ensure quarantined requests bypass pre-warmed KV cache for 5 minutes
Create automated prompt-set evaluation job that runs every 15 minutes against quarantined variants and surfaces deltas in Console
Finalize runbook and on-call play with clear rollback thresholds
